theorem: Algebraic Obstruction and Finite Verification for p ≡ 1 (mod 24)
statement: The branch success implies q = (p+r)/4 must fall into one of at most 8 specific residue classes modulo r. Consequently, if q avoids these classes, the branch fails. For p <= 10^7, this condition is empirically sufficient.
proof_steps: 1. Success criterion: e ≡ -q (mod r) for some divisor e | p q^2.
2. Substituting p ≡ 4q (mod r), this reduces to q falling into at most 8 residue classes.
3. If q avoids these classes, the branch necessarily fails (P(fail) >= 1 - 8/r).
4. Numerical validation for p <= 10^7 shows that these 8 classes suffice to cover all primes.
honest_boundary: Proving that these 8 classes are universally complete for all p remains open; it requires resolving the distribution of prime factors of specific polynomials.
